title: Etale descent of pseudo-coherence
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\epsilon_X:(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}})\to(X_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathcal O_X)$ the canonical morphism of ringed sites, with tensor module pullback $\epsilon_X^*$ [lem-trf-zariski-etale-functor-comparison-square]. Let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ be arbitrary. Use unbounded derived categories of sheaves of modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. A strictly perfect complex is a bounded complex whose terms are direct summands of finite free structure modules. On a ringed site, an object $K$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent if locally on every object of the site there are a strictly perfect complex $P^\bullet$ and a map $P^\bullet\to K$ in the derived category inducing isomorphisms on $H^j$ for $j>m$ and a surjection on $H^m$; it is pseudo-coherent if this holds for every integer $m$. For every $m\in\mathbf Z$, $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent on $X_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ if and only if $\epsilon_X^*E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$. In particular $E$ is pseudo-coherent if and only if $\epsilon_X^*E$ is pseudo-coherent. No quasi-coherence or global boundedness is assumed.

proof.text: For every open subscheme $U\subseteq X$, the module functor $\epsilon_U^*$ is exact and faithful on all modules, not just quasi-coherent ones. Its termwise extension defines a triangulated functor on unbounded derived categories. Exactness gives $H^j(\epsilon_U^*K)=\epsilon_U^*H^j(K)$: kernels, images and their quotient are preserved. Thus it detects cohomology vanishing. We use these identifications on each open below.

source.place: Tag 08HE (lemma-descend-pseudo-coherent), first paragraph, exactness and the cohomology identity; Tag 08H8.

proof.text: For the forward implication take the local strictly perfect approximations on a Zariski open cover. Their pullbacks are strictly perfect: tensor pullback sends $\mathcal O$ to the target structure module, preserves finite sums and sends a retraction $pi=1$ to the same retraction identity. The cohomology identity in step 1 preserves the required isomorphisms and surjection. The same open cover is an etale cover, and its base changes cover every etale object. Hence these are the required approximations to $\epsilon_X^*E$.

source.place: Tag 08HE (lemma-descend-pseudo-coherent), first paragraph, implication (1) to (2); flat pullback of the defining approximations.

proof.text: For the converse work on an affine open $U\subseteq X$; the property to prove is local by its definition. Choose an etale cover of $U$ carrying the strictly perfect approximations to $\epsilon_U^*(E|_U)$. Their cohomology vanishes above their respective finite upper bounds and above $m$. Etale maps have open images, so quasi-compactness of the affine $U$ selects finitely many of these images covering $U$. Take $N$ to be the maximum of $m-1$ and those finitely many bounds. Cohomology sheaves of the pullback vanish above $N$, since they vanish on this cover. By step 1 the same holds for $E|_U$. If $U$ is empty the assertion is vacuous. This obtains only a bound on the chosen open, without imposing a global bound.

source.place: Tag 08HE (lemma-descend-pseudo-coherent), second paragraph, local quasi-compact reduction and boundedness above.

proof.text: Fix $m$. Prove, simultaneously for all schemes and all complexes with a chosen upper cohomology bound $N$, that an $m$-pseudo-coherent etale pullback implies $m$-pseudo-coherence on the Zariski site. Induct on $\max(0,N-m+1)$. When $N<m$, the map $0\to E$ is a strictly perfect approximation: the cohomology above $m$ and in degree $m$ is zero. The same argument handles the zero complex without choosing a largest nonzero degree. In the remaining case $N\geq m$, put $n=N$.

source.place: Tag 08HE (lemma-descend-pseudo-coherent), third paragraph, induction, with an upper bound instead of a largest nonzero degree.

proof.text: The pullback is also $n$-pseudo-coherent: its $m$-approximation is an isomorphism in degrees $>n$ and is surjective in degree $n$ (an isomorphism there if $n>m$). Its cohomology vanishes above $n$. The ringed-site top-cohomology lemma therefore makes $H^n(\epsilon_X^*E)$ finite type. Step 1 identifies this with $\epsilon_X^*H^n(E)$; finite-type detection gives finite type of $H^n(E)$ on $X$. After a Zariski open cover choose a surjection $q:\mathcal O_X^{\oplus t}\twoheadrightarrow H^n(E)$ with finite $t$; we continue on each such open.

source.place: Tag 08HE (lemma-descend-pseudo-coherent), third paragraph, finite type of the highest cohomology and a finite set of generators.

proof.text: Represent $E$ by a complex $A^\bullet$. Apply local lifting from a finite free module to the epimorphism $Z^n(A)\twoheadrightarrow H^n(A)$ and to $q$. The Zariski site and all its slices have the required module sheafification and local-bijectivity descriptions. On a further open cover obtain $b:\mathcal O_X^{\oplus t}\to Z^n(A)$ inducing $q$. Composing with $Z^n(A)\hookrightarrow A^n$ gives a chain map $\alpha:\mathcal O_X^{\oplus t}[-n]\to A^\bullet$, since $d^nb=0$. Complete it to a distinguished triangle $P\to E\to C\to P[1]$, where $P=\mathcal O_X^{\oplus t}[-n]$. In its long exact cohomology sequence, for $j>n$ the neighbours of $H^j(C)$ vanish, while for $j=n$ the surjection $H^n(P)\twoheadrightarrow H^n(E)$ has next term $H^{n+1}(P)=0$. Hence $H^j(C)=0$ for every $j\geq n$.

source.place: Tag 08HE (lemma-descend-pseudo-coherent), third paragraph, the omitted local lift, and the cohomology of its cone.

proof.text: The one-term complex $P$ is strictly perfect, so its identity makes it $a$-pseudo-coherent for every integer $a$. Its etale pullback has the same property. Pull back the distinguished triangle using step 1. Part (1) of the ringed-site triangle lemma, with $K=\epsilon_X^*P$, $L=\epsilon_X^*E$, gives that $\epsilon_X^*C$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. The bound for $C$ is $n-1$, so the induction measure drops by one; apply the induction hypothesis on every current open to deduce that $C$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. Part (2) of the triangle lemma on the Zariski site, with $K=P$, $L=E$, $M=C$, now gives that $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent there. The defining local approximations combine over the successive open covers, proving the converse for the original $X$.

source.place: Tag 08HE (lemma-descend-pseudo-coherent), final paragraph, cone pseudo-coherence, induction, and reconstruction of E.

proof.text: The argument applies separately to every $m\in\mathbf Z$. Taking the conjunction over all integers gives the claimed equivalence for pseudo-coherence, by its definition. The affine reduction and its upper bound were chosen locally; none of the steps assumed quasi-coherence or a global boundedness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 08HE (lemma-descend-pseudo-coherent), consequence for pseudo-coherence in all degrees.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q125-72f6eccc7 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks 08HE, 08HD and 08H8 in spaces-perfect.tex, and 08FT, 08FU, 08FV, 08FX and lemma-local-lift-map in sites-cohomology.tex, in full. The item statement is byte-identical to the base and matches 08HE: any scheme, arbitrary E, fixed m, no quasi-coherence. The base had no proof, so this is a first split, not a re-split. Step 1 uses only the 'exact and faithful on all module sheaves' sentence of lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence, together with the exact-functor derived factorization. Step 2 writes out the forward direction without 08H4, using pullback of strictly perfect complexes and Zariski covers being étale covers. Step 3 gets a local bound on an affine open from étale-open images and quasi-compactness. Step 4 sets up an explicit induction on max(0,N-m+1) whose base case N<m covers E=0; this correctly repairs Stacks' 'largest n'. Step 5 applies 08FX(1) with index n (I checked that m-pc implies n-pc) and then 08HD for arbitrary modules; it correctly avoids the quasi-coherent fpqc descent node. Step 6 fills in the 'details omitted' cycle lift via lem-sf-site-finite-projective-lift (M=Z^n, N=H^n, g=q), and I checked the long exact sequence argument that H^j(C)=0 for j>=n. Step 7 uses 08FV(1) on the étale side and 08FV(2) on the Zariski side, with the shifts verified; the induction measure drops. The three new nodes are 08HD (arbitrary modules), 08FX(1) and 08FV(1-3) for a general ringed site. They are statement-only, self-contained and true; I tested them on zero objects, one-term free complexes and non-coherent quotients. I grepped the DAG and found only ring or scheme variants (064R, 064S, 08CD, 08DN(2)), so none is a duplicate and none restates the item. Route: finite-projective-lift is in the cited unit sk-thm-sf-hom-ctf; the other tools are Mathlib leaves. Batch-5 finding: lem-trf-zariski-etale-functor-comparison-square is the generic Descent 03FH/03LC change-of-topology square, used only to name ε and ε^*. The item and lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence already cite it the same way, it is not part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, and so I did not return for it. No SGA. Advisory only: the generic ringed-site nodes omit def-weil-size-convention.
